title: Ionic Bond, Lattice Enthalpy Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Salt only melts at 801 °C, while sugar melts in a pan in minutes. What holds salt together so tightly? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we follow the ionic bond from start to finish.

You will see a tug of war for one electron, add up the energy on the molecule bench (+495.8 kJ/mol to make Na+, -348.7 kJ/mol when Cl takes the electron, still 147.1 short), and watch the ions click into a crystal lattice that releases 788 kJ/mol. We define lattice enthalpy step by step, see why bigger charges and smaller ions make it larger, compare NaCl with MgO, and cover the Born-Haber steps and properties of ionic solids asked by ISC. Then the exam trap, an original JEE and NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 39 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:

2:41 The lattice pays for the ions
2:47 Worked example: NaCl vs MgO
3:23 Born-Haber steps and properties (ISC)
